chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Nuʿaym ibn Ibrahim, from Mismaʿ ibn ʿAbd al-Malik, from Abi ʿAbdillah عليه السلام, who said:

“The offense of an umm al-walad, regarding the rights of people, is upon her master; and whatever is from the rights of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in the prescribed punishments, then that is upon her body.” He said: “Retaliation is taken from her for the slaves, and there is no qisas between the free person and the slave.”

key_terms.أُمُّ الْوَلَدِ: A slave woman who has borne a child to her master.
key_terms.الْحُدُودِ: The fixed prescribed punishments in sacred law.
key_terms.جِنَايَتُهَا: Her offense or legal injury entailing liability.
key_terms.حُقُوقِ اللَّهِ: The rights of Allah, referring here to divinely prescribed penal matters.
key_terms.حُقُوقِ النَّاسِ: The rights owed to people in cases of harm or liability.
key_terms.قِصَاصَ: Legal retaliation in kind for injury or killing.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the offense of an umm al-walad and qisas between a free person and a slave?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out a legal ruling concerning the liability of an umm al-walad in matters involving the rights of people and the rights of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It distinguishes between financial or civil responsibility borne by the master and bodily punishments that apply to her personally, while also clarifying rulings of qisas involving slaves and free persons.
